blocks.text: Imagine searching for a word in a dictionary. Instead of flipping through every page, you start in the middle, decide which half to search next, and repeat. This is the essence of binary search.

blocks.markdown: Binary search is an efficient algorithm for finding an item in a sorted array. It works by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half. If the value of the search key is less than the item in the middle of the interval, the search continues in the lower half, or if greater, in the upper half. This process continues until the item is found or the interval is empty.

blocks.title: Binary Search
blocks.text: Binary search is an algorithm that finds the position of a target value within a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.

blocks.markdown: To implement binary search, we maintain two pointers, `low` and `high`, which represent the current bounds of the search interval. The algorithm proceeds by calculating the midpoint of the interval and comparing the middle element to the target value.

blocks.title: Implementing Binary Search
blocks.prompt: Implement binary search on a sorted array to find the index of a target value.

steps.text: Initialize `low` to 0 and `high` to the last index of the array.
While `low` is less than or equal to `high`, compute `mid` as the floor of `(low + high) / 2`.
If the middle element is equal to the target, return `mid`.
If the middle element is less than the target, set `low` to `mid + 1`.
If the middle element is greater than the target, set `high` to `mid - 1`.
If the loop exits without finding the target, return -1 to indicate the target is not in the array.

blocks.answer: The binary search algorithm efficiently finds the index of the target value or returns -1 if not found.

blocks.title: Loop Invariant
blocks.text: The loop invariant for binary search is that the target value, if it exists, is always within the current `low` and `high` bounds.

blocks.markdown: The correctness of binary search relies on maintaining the loop invariant. At each step, the algorithm ensures that the target value is within the bounds defined by `low` and `high`. This invariant holds true before, during, and after each iteration of the loop.

blocks.title: Example of Binary Search
blocks.prompt: Perform binary search on the array [1, 3, 5, 7, 9] to find the index of the target value 5.

steps.text: The middle element at index 2 is 5, which matches the target value.

blocks.answer: The target value 5 is found at index 2.

blocks.markdown: Binary search is efficient with a time complexity of $O(\log n)$, where $n$ is the number of elements in the array. However, it requires the array to be sorted beforehand. If the array is not sorted, sorting it first would take $O(n \log n)$ time.

blocks.title: Sorted Input Requirement
blocks.text: Binary search only works on sorted arrays. If the array is unsorted, it must be sorted first, which impacts the overall time complexity.

points: Binary search efficiently finds a target in a sorted array by halving the search interval.
The loop invariant ensures the target is within the current bounds.
Binary search requires a sorted array, and sorting impacts the overall efficiency.
